what_it_checks: that a configured retry budget really re-issues the upstream call on the listed status, and that exhausting the budget without success is reported as the sentinel attempt count rather than the real number of tries
that exceeding the per-attempt timeout produces a synthesised timeout response instead of waiting for the provider
that an explicit retry budget and status list are preserved, and that with no retry block the default is zero attempts with an empty status list: retries are off unless asked for
the precedence order for the per-attempt timeout: the request header beats the target's own setting, and it is absent when neither supplies one
that a lookup against remembered state returns an explicit disabled result when the endpoint is not cacheable or no store is configured, rather than silently behaving as a miss

that the spend-veto seam is a no-op when nothing is installed, and short-circuits the request with its own answer when something is: the executable statement that this gateway has no cost policy of its own
that every response carries the address of the serving config node, the trace identifier, the attempt count, the cache status and the provider name
that a quality-check span is created per provider attempt and that its verdicts drive the deny and check-failed outcomes
